title: Java I/O and NIO.2 Quick Revision
summary: Fast revision of Java file I/O: byte vs character streams, try-with-resources, BufferedReader, java.nio.file Path and Files, encodings and directory walking.

chapters.title: Java I/O Mental Model
points: Byte streams (InputStream/OutputStream) move raw 8-bit data: use for images, PDFs, zips, any binary
Character streams (Reader/Writer) move 16-bit chars and decode/encode bytes via a charset: use for text
Bridge classes InputStreamReader/OutputStreamWriter wrap a byte stream with an explicit Charset to get a character stream
Decorator pattern: wrap streams in layers, e.g. new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(new FileInputStream(f), UTF_8))
Mistake: using a Reader on binary data corrupts it, since decoding replaces invalid bytes

chapters.title: try-with-resources and BufferedReader
points: try (var r = new BufferedReader(...)) { } auto-closes any AutoCloseable, even when an exception is thrown
Multiple resources close in reverse order of declaration; closing the outer wrapper closes the inner stream
Exceptions from close() are attached as suppressed exceptions, retrievable via getSuppressed(), so the primary exception is not lost
BufferedReader.readLine() returns null at end of file and strips the line terminator; loop: while ((line = br.readLine()) != null)
Buffering cuts system calls by reading chunks (default 8192 chars); BufferedWriter needs newLine() or flush(), and flush happens on close

chapters.title: Path and Files Essentials
points: Path is an immutable location object created by Path.of("a","b.txt") or Paths.get; it may not exist on disk
Path operations are pure string logic: resolve(other) appends, relativize(other) computes the relative path, normalize() removes . and .., toAbsolutePath() anchors to cwd
Files.exists/notExists/isDirectory/size/delete/deleteIfExists/createDirectories/copy/move are the everyday checks and actions
Files.copy and Files.move throw FileAlreadyExistsException unless you pass StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING; ATOMIC_MOVE requests an atomic rename
java.io.File is legacy: it returns booleans on failure instead of exceptions; prefer Path and Files, convert with file.toPath() or path.toFile()

chapters.title: Reading and Writing Files
points: Small files: String s = Files.readString(p); List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(p); byte[] b = Files.readAllBytes(p); all load everything into memory
Large files: try (Stream<String> s = Files.lines(p)) { } is lazy, and the stream must be closed
Write: Files.writeString(p, text) or Files.write(p, lines); the default truncates and creates the file
Append with StandardOpenOption.APPEND (combine with CREATE); use CREATE_NEW to fail if the file exists
Streaming with a chosen charset: Files.newBufferedReader(p, UTF_8) and Files.newBufferedWriter(p, UTF_8, options) wrapped in try-with-resources

chapters.title: Character Encodings and Directory Walking
points: A charset maps characters to bytes; UTF-8 is variable length (1 to 4 bytes), ISO-8859-1 is 1 byte per char, UTF-16 is 2 or 4 bytes
new FileReader(f) used the platform default charset before Java 18; since Java 18 (JEP 400) the default is UTF-8, but always pass StandardCharsets.UTF_8 explicitly
Files.readString, writeString and newBufferedReader default to UTF-8 and throw MalformedInputException on invalid bytes, while InputStreamReader silently substitutes U+FFFD
Files.list(dir) is a one-level lazy Stream<Path>; Files.walk(dir, maxDepth) recurses; both hold directory handles so close them with try-with-resources

Files.find(dir, depth, (p, attrs) -> ...) filters with attributes cheaply; for full control use Files.walkFileTree with a SimpleFileVisitor (visitFile, preVisitDirectory, postVisitDirectory), the standard way to delete a directory tree recursively

chapters.title: Java File I/O Cheat Sheet
points: Binary = InputStream/OutputStream; text = Reader/Writer with an explicit charset
Always try-with-resources; resources close in reverse order and close() errors become suppressed
Small file: Files.readString / readAllLines; large file: Files.lines or newBufferedReader in try-with-resources
Write modes: default truncate+create; APPEND adds; CREATE_NEW fails if present; REPLACE_EXISTING for copy/move
Walk: Files.list (1 level), Files.walk (recursive), walkFileTree (control and delete trees); close the streams
